DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1-1.note: rfc_mup_ingress_test.go drives nlritype.Get(fam)+nlritype.Retain, the call typedNLRIEdit (reactor/session_validation_nlritype.go) makes at ingress. Positive TestMUPOtherRouteTypesSilentlyIgnoredAtIngress: route types 0/5/99/0xFFFF under arch 1 dropped (dropped==4), no error, ISD kept byte for byte, both AFIs; red on a recognizer that keeps them or on an error. Negative TestMUPDefinedRouteTypesSurviveIngress: types 1..4 kept whole, red on an over-broad ignore. The older ParseMUP positive (TestRFCMUPUnknownRouteTypeIsNotRejected) proves only the decode path skips the NLRI by its Length; it adds no clause. 'silently' is proven as no error from Retain; the Debug log line in typedNLRIEdit is not asserted, and the RFC 7606 Section 6 log is not a violation of silent ignore at protocol level. Revert records observed red for each unit

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-10.note: asserts ParseMUP returns ErrMUPTLV for a TLV Length overrun on the decode path; nothing asserts Treat-as-withdraw, and ingress never walks TLVs, so the route is stored

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-6.note: asserts ParseMUP returns ErrMUPTruncated, which is the decode path (DecodeNLRIHex, RunCLIDecode); nothing asserts Treat-as-withdraw, and ingress (SplitMUP framing, RecognizeNLRI arch/route type) stores such a route, so the test would stay green with the MUST unmet

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-7.note: asserts ParseMUP returns ErrMUPTLV for one leftover octet on the decode path; nothing asserts Treat-as-withdraw, and ingress (SplitMUP framing, RecognizeNLRI arch/route type) never validates TLVs, so the route is stored

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.3.1-9.note: Propagate clause: TestMUPUnknownTLVPropagatedUnchangedAtIngress asserts the section kept by nlritype.Retain with the registered recognizer (the section typedNLRIEdit relays) equals the received T1ST with unknown TLV 0xF0, both unchanged and when a sibling unknown route type forces the rebuild; red on any re-encode that strips or rewrites the TLV. Local-processing clause: ParseMUP of the kept route yields the TEID and endpoint of the TLV-less route (and TestMUPT1STUnknownTLVIgnoredAndPropagated pins prefix, bits, TEID, QFI, endpoint, and that only a framing error refuses). Negatives: TestMUPUnknownTLVNotStrippedAtIngress pins length +5, Length octet +5, trailing TLV octets; the tlv_mup_test negative pins Bytes() is not the TLV-less form. The negatives are the complement of the positives' byte equality rather than an independent input, acceptable for a propagate-unchanged obligation. Records observed red for every unit (Retain, validateTLVs, ParseMUP)

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.1.4.1-3.note: Encoder (the sender side the MUST NOT binds): TestMUPT2STEncoderKeepsEndpointLengthWithinTEID asserts EncodeNLRIHex writes Endpoint Length address bits + 0/16/32 (32 default) for IPv4 and IPv6; TestMUPT2STEncoderRefusesEndpointLengthBeyondTEID asserts teid bits 33 and 40 (v4, v6), -8 and unreadable are refused with errTeidBits. Author observed all five negatives red on HEAD's parseTEIDWithBits (D-8 defect fixed in encode.go, re-checked at the producer: both callers propagate the error). Decode path: TestMUPT2STEndpointLengthBoundedByTEID, 64 parses, 72 refused ErrMUPEndpointTooLong. Not covered here: ingress (RecognizeNLRI) does not refuse an over-long Endpoint Length from a peer, so such a route is stored and relayed; that receive handling is the Section 3.1.4 malformed rule (3.1.4-1, a disclosed {gap}), not this sentence

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.3.6-4.note: Read RecognizeNLRI (rfc7606.go): it reads architecture and route type only, and typedNLRIEdit passes it the NLRI section alone. No code in internal/component/bgp reads a Prefix-SID locator or compares a DSD MP_REACH next hop with it (reactor Prefix-SID code handles RFC 8669 Section 8 egress only), so a DSD route with a mismatched next hop is stored, not treated as withdraw. The {gap} annotation and Meta row disclose it

DRAFT-IETF-BESS-MUP-SAFI-3.3.6-5.note: Read RecognizeNLRI (rfc7606.go) and its caller typedNLRIEdit: the ingress pass judges each MUP NLRI by architecture and route type, never consults the UPDATE's path attributes, and session_validation.go has no MUP or Prefix-SID presence rule, so a DSD route arriving without a Prefix-SID attribute is stored, not treated as withdraw. The {gap} annotation and Meta row disclose it
